284	# --- Anthropic-specific quirks: mid-list system folding ---
285	
286	
287	_MID_SYSTEM_WRAP_PREFIX = "<system-reminder>\n"
288	_MID_SYSTEM_WRAP_SUFFIX = "\n</system-reminder>\n"
289	
290	
291	def _fold_mid_list_system_into_user(body_obj: dict) -> bool:
292	    """Fold non-leading role:system messages into a neighbouring user message as
293	    a <system-reminder> text block. Mutates body_obj in place; returns True iff
294	    any fold happened.
295	
296	    Some clients insert a system message in the middle of the message list, but
297	    many chat templates reject any system message past index 0. Attaching the
298	    wrapped reminder to the preceding user message (or the next one, if there is
299	    no prior user message) keeps the history acceptable to the template.
300	    """
301	    msgs = body_obj.get("messages")
302	    if not isinstance(msgs, list) or not msgs:
303	        return False
304	
305	    system_idx = [i for i, m in enumerate(msgs) if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") == "system" and i > 0]
306	    if not system_idx:
307	        return False
308	
309	    def _promote_to_list(msg: dict) -> list:
310	        c = msg.get("content")
311	        if isinstance(c, list):
312	            return c
313	        msg["content"] = [{"type": "text", "text": c if isinstance(c, str) else ""}]
314	        return msg["content"]
315	
316	    def _wrap(text: str) -> dict:
317	        return {
318	            "type": "text",
319	            "text": _MID_SYSTEM_WRAP_PREFIX + text + _MID_SYSTEM_WRAP_SUFFIX,
320	        }
321	
322	    changed = False
323	    TOMBSTONE: dict = {"__folded__": True}
324	    for i in system_idx:
325	        sys_msg = msgs[i]
326	        wrapped = _wrap(flatten_content(sys_msg.get("content")))
327	        target = None
328	        for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
329	            cand = msgs[j]
330	            if isinstance(cand, dict) and cand.get("role") == "user":
331	                target = cand
332	                _promote_to_list(target).append(wrapped)
333	                break
334	        if target is None:
335	            for j in range(i + 1, len(msgs)):
336	                cand = msgs[j]
337	                if isinstance(cand, dict) and cand.get("role") == "user":
338	                    target = cand
339	                    _promote_to_list(target).insert(0, wrapped)
340	                    break
341	        if target is None:
342	            msgs[i] = {"role": "user", "content": [wrapped]}
343	            changed = True
344	            continue
345	        msgs[i] = TOMBSTONE
346	        changed = True
347	
348	    if changed:
349	        body_obj["messages"] = [m for m in msgs if m is not TOMBSTONE]
350	    return changed
351

1	"""OpenAI Chat-Completions adapter for agent rollouts.
2	
3	Mirrors slime.agent.adapters.anthropic but speaks the OpenAI
4	/v1/chat/completions protocol, so an OpenAI-compatible client (e.g. the Codex
5	CLI) can drive the slime sglang server. Each request is rendered with the served
6	model's chat template, sent to sglang /generate as input_ids, parsed, and folded
7	into a shared TrajectoryManager keyed by session id. finish_session(sid) drains
8	a session's trajectory into a list of Sample.
9	
10	Only /v1/chat/completions is implemented; the Responses API (/v1/responses) is
11	out of scope. The section layout (adapter class -> translation -> reply building
12	-> request framing) mirrors slime.agent.adapters.anthropic.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import json
18	import logging
19	import secrets
20	import time
21	from typing import Any
22	
23	from aiohttp import web
24	
25	from slime.agent.adapters.common import (
26	    BaseAdapter,
27	    Reply,
28	    flatten_content,
29	    manager_finish_reason,
30	    sid_from_bearer,
31	    sid_from_body,
32	)
33	from slime.agent.parsing import ParsedModelOutput
34	
35	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
36	
37	
38	class OpenAIAdapter(BaseAdapter):
39	    """OpenAI Chat-Completions-compatible HTTP adapter: wire translation and
40	    reply framing only; the turn machinery is inherited from BaseAdapter."""
41	
42	    logger = logger
43	    log_prefix = "openai_adapter"
44	    max_token_keys = ("max_completion_tokens", "max_tokens", "max_output_tokens")
45	    stop_keys = ("stop",)
46	
47	    def _register_routes(self, app: web.Application) -> None:
48	        app.router.add_post("/v1/chat/completions", self._run_turn)
49	
50	    def _session_id(self, request: web.Request, body: dict) -> str:
51	        return _request_session_id(request, body)
52	
53	    def _translate(self, body: dict) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict] | None]:
54	        messages = body.get("messages") or []
55	        if not isinstance(messages, list):
56	            raise web.HTTPBadRequest(text="messages must be a list")
57	        translated = _translate_messages(messages)
58	        tools_schema = _tools_to_chat_tools(body.get("tools"))
59	        return translated, tools_schema
60	
61	    def _build_reply(self, parsed, raw_finish, translated, tools_schema) -> Reply:
62	        wire_message, manager_message, wire_finish = _build_reply_parts(parsed, raw_finish)
63	        return Reply(
64	            manager_message=manager_message,
65	            finish_reason=manager_finish_reason(parsed.tool_uses, raw_finish),
66	            wire=(wire_message, wire_finish),
67	        )
68	
69	    async def _respond(self, request, body, reply, in_tok, out_tok, stream) -> web.StreamResponse:
70	        wire_message, wire_finish = reply.wire
71	        if stream:
72	            return await _render_stream(request, body, wire_message, wire_finish, in_tok, out_tok)
73	        return web.json_response(_render_response(body, wire_message, wire_finish, in_tok, out_tok))
74	
75	
76	# --- Translation (OpenAI wire -> chat-template messages) ---
77	
78	
79	def _arguments_as_dict(arguments: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
80	    """Coerce wire-shape tool_calls[].function.arguments into a dict.
81	
82	    OpenAI sends arguments as a JSON-encoded string; the chat template and the
83	    trajectory manager's history matching both expect a mapping. Malformed
84	    payloads fall back to {"_raw_arguments": s}.
85	    """
86	    if isinstance(arguments, dict):
87	        return arguments
88	    if arguments is None:
89	        return {}
90	    if isinstance(arguments, str):
91	        s = arguments.strip()
92	        if not s:
93	            return {}
94	        try:
95	            parsed = json.loads(s)
96	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
97	            return {"_raw_arguments": arguments}
98	        return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {"_raw_arguments": arguments}
99	    return {"_raw_arguments": str(arguments)}
100	
101	
102	def _translate_messages(messages: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
103	    """OpenAI chat messages -> tokenizer chat-template messages.
104	
105	    Mirrors anthropic._translate_messages so a replayed assistant turn compares
106	    equal (dict equality) to the leaf the manager appended on the previous
107	    request. Two invariants must hold:
108	
109	      * tool_calls[i].function.arguments is a dict (not a JSON string): the chat
110	        template needs a mapping, and the manager matches history by dict
111	        equality regardless of key order.
112	      * Wire-only correlation ids are dropped (tool_call_id on tool messages,
113	        tool_calls[i].id on echoed assistant messages). Fresh ids are minted on
114	        each response, so keeping the wire ids would diverge the replay match.
115	    """
116	    translated: list[dict] = []
117	    for msg in messages:
118	        if not isinstance(msg, dict):
119	            continue
120	        role = msg.get("role")
121	        content = msg.get("content")
122	        if role == "developer":  # OpenAI Responses API alias
123	            role = "system"
124	
125	        if role in {"system", "user"}:
126	            translated.append({"role": role, "content": flatten_content(content)})
127	        elif role == "tool":
128	            # drop tool_call_id -- wire-only correlation field; see docstring
129	            translated.append({"role": "tool", "content": flatten_content(content)})
130	        elif role == "assistant":
131	            assistant: dict[str, Any] = {
132	                "role": "assistant",
133	                "content": flatten_content(content),
134	            }
135	            reasoning = msg.get("reasoning_content")
136	            if reasoning:
137	                assistant["reasoning_content"] = reasoning
138	            tool_calls = msg.get("tool_calls") or []
139	            normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
140	            for call in tool_calls:
141	                if not isinstance(call, dict):
142	                    continue
143	                function = call.get("function") or {}
144	                name = function.get("name") or call.get("name") or "tool"
145	                arguments = function.get("arguments")
146	                if arguments is None:
147	                    arguments = call.get("arguments", {})
148	                # NB: arguments stays a dict (not a JSON string), and the
149	                # wire-only id is dropped. See docstring above.
150	                normalized.append(
151	                    {
152	                        "type": "function",
153	                        "function": {
154	                            "name": name,
155	                            "arguments": _arguments_as_dict(arguments),
156	                        },
157	                    }
158	                )
159	            if normalized:
160	                assistant["tool_calls"] = normalized
161	            translated.append(assistant)
162	        # unknown roles are silently dropped
163	    return translated
164	
165	
166	def _tools_to_chat_tools(tools: list[dict] | None) -> list[dict] | None:
167	    """Convert OpenAI tools list to tokenizer chat-template tool schema."""
168	    if not tools:
169	        return None
170	    normalized: list[dict] = []
171	    for tool in tools:
172	        if not isinstance(tool, dict):
173	            continue
174	        if tool.get("type") and tool.get("type") != "function":
175	            continue
176	        function = tool.get("function") if isinstance(tool.get("function"), dict) else None
177	        if function is not None:
178	            name = function.get("name")
179	            if not name:
180	                continue
181	            normalized.append(
182	                {
183	                    "type": "function",
184	                    "function": {
185	                        "name": name,
186	                        "description": function.get("description", ""),
187	                        "parameters": function.get("parameters") or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
188	                    },
189	                }
190	            )
191	        else:
192	            name = tool.get("name")
193	            if not name:
194	                continue
195	            normalized.append(
196	                {
197	                    "type": "function",
198	                    "function": {
199	                        "name": name,
200	                        "description": tool.get("description", ""),
201	                        "parameters": tool.get("parameters") or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
202	                    },
203	                }
204	            )
205	    return normalized or None
206	
207	
208	# --- Reply building: parsed output -> OpenAI wire message + manager_message ---
209	
210	
211	def _build_reply_parts(parsed: ParsedModelOutput, finish: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any], str]:
212	    """Return (wire_message, manager_message, wire_finish).
213	
214	    wire_message follows the OpenAI Chat-Completions spec: tool_calls[].id is a
215	    unique correlation id and tool_calls[].function.arguments is a JSON-encoded
216	    string (clients depend on this).
217	
218	    manager_message is the shape fed to record_turn: arguments is a dict so
219	    chat-template replay succeeds and the manager's history match (dict equality)
220	    holds against the echo on the next turn, and the wire-only id is omitted.
221	    """
222	    wire_tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
223	    manager_tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
224	    for tu in parsed.tool_uses:
225	        name = tu.get("name", "tool")
226	        args_dict = tu.get("input") or {}
227	        if not isinstance(args_dict, dict):
228	            args_dict = {"_raw_arguments": str(args_dict)}
229	        call_id = f"call_{secrets.token_hex(12)}"
230	        wire_tool_calls.append(
231	            {
232	                "id": call_id,
233	                "type": "function",
234	                "function": {
235	                    "name": name,
236	                    "arguments": json.dumps(args_dict, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True),
237	                },
238	            }
239	        )
240	        manager_tool_calls.append(
241	            {
242	                "type": "function",
243	                "function": {
244	                    "name": name,
245	                    "arguments": args_dict,
246	                },
247	            }
248	        )
249	
250	    wire_message: dict[str, Any] = {
251	        "role": "assistant",
252	        # send content=null when there are tool_calls: some OpenAI clients split
253	        # a mixed text+tool_calls turn into two echoed messages otherwise, which
254	        # diverges the history match against our leaf
255	        "content": None if wire_tool_calls else (parsed.text or None),
256	    }
257	    # manager_message must match what the client echoes on the next request, or
258	    # the manager's history match (dict equality) diverges and every turn forks.
259	    # Differences from wire_message, each needed to match the echo:
260	    #   * no reasoning_content -- some clients strip it on echo (the reasoning
261	    #     token ids are still kept in the trained tokens, only the text drops)
262	    #   * only the first tool_call -- some clients drop extra parallel tool_calls
263	    #   * empty content when tool_calls are present -- mirrors content=null above
264	    manager_message: dict[str, Any] = {
265	        "role": "assistant",
266	        "content": "" if wire_tool_calls else (parsed.text or ""),
267	    }
268	    if parsed.reasoning:
269	        wire_message["reasoning_content"] = parsed.reasoning
270	    if wire_tool_calls:
271	        wire_message["tool_calls"] = wire_tool_calls[:1]
272	        manager_message["tool_calls"] = manager_tool_calls[:1]
273	
274	    if parsed.tool_uses:
275	        wire_finish = "tool_calls"
276	    elif finish == "length":
277	        wire_finish = "length"
278	    else:
279	        wire_finish = "stop"
280	
281	    return wire_message, manager_message, wire_finish
282

324	async def _render_stream(
325	    request: web.Request,
326	    body: dict,
327	    wire_message: dict[str, Any],
328	    wire_finish: str,
329	    in_tok: int,
330	    out_tok: int,
331	) -> web.StreamResponse:
332	    """Emit the OpenAI Chat-Completions SSE stream.
333	
334	    Each chunk has the shape `data: {chatcmpl ...}\n\n`, ending with
335	    `data: [DONE]`. The whole turn is realised on the server before streaming
336	    (we have no token-level deltas from sglang here), so we emit one role chunk,
337	    then content / reasoning / tool_calls in single delta chunks each.
338	    """
339	    out = web.StreamResponse(
340	        status=200,
341	        headers={
342	            "Content-Type": "text/event-stream",
343	            "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
344	            "Connection": "keep-alive",
345	        },
346	    )
347	    await out.prepare(request)
348	    completion_id = f"chatcmpl_{secrets.token_hex(12)}"
349	    created = int(time.time())
350	
351	    async def emit(delta: dict[str, Any], finish_reason: str | None = None, usage: dict | None = None) -> None:
352	        chunk = {
353	            "id": completion_id,
354	            "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
355	            "created": created,
356	            "model": body.get("model", "slime-actor"),
357	            "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": delta, "finish_reason": finish_reason}],
358	        }
359	        if usage is not None:
360	            chunk["usage"] = usage
361	        await out.write(f"data: {json.dumps(chunk, ensure_ascii=False)}\n\n".encode())
362	
363	    await emit({"role": "assistant"})
364	    reasoning = wire_message.get("reasoning_content")
365	    if reasoning:
366	        await emit({"reasoning_content": reasoning})
367	    content = wire_message.get("content")
368	    if content:
369	        await emit({"content": content})
370	    # emit all tool_calls in a single chunk: some clients accumulate per-index
371	    # arguments fragments across chunks, collapsing N parallel tool_calls into
372	    # one call with a concatenated (and unparseable) arguments string
373	    tool_calls = wire_message.get("tool_calls") or []
374	    if tool_calls:
375	        await emit({"tool_calls": [{**call, "index": idx} for idx, call in enumerate(tool_calls)]})
376	    await emit({}, finish_reason=wire_finish, usage=_usage(in_tok, out_tok))
377	    await out.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
378	    return out
379

1	"""Build a per-session training trajectory from multi-turn conversation data.
2	
3	The :class:`TrajectoryManager` builds one trajectory per session. ``record_turn``
4	feeds in each turn (prompt messages + the served model's sglang snapshot),
5	routing it into a per-sid message tree; ``get_trajectory`` then linearizes that
6	tree into a ``list[Sample]`` of loss-masked training rows, tolerating TITO
7	re-tokenization drift via fork/replace.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import dataclasses
13	import enum
14	import logging
15	from collections.abc import Iterator
16	from typing import Any
17	
18	from slime.utils.types import Sample
19	
20	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
21	
22	
23	# ===========================================================================
24	# TurnRecord
25	# ===========================================================================
26	
27	
28	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
29	class TurnRecord:
30	    """One sglang ``/generate`` snapshot: the contract between an adapter and the
31	    manager. Adapters build it from a turn's prompt/output token ids; ``record_turn``
32	    consumes it."""
33	
34	    prompt_ids: list[int]
35	    output_ids: list[int]
36	    finish_reason: str
37	    output_log_probs: list[float] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
38	    ill_formed: bool = False
39	
40	
41	# ===========================================================================
42	# MessageNode
43	# ===========================================================================
44	
45	
46	class MessageNode:
47	    """One node in a session's routing tree, carrying a single chat message
48	    (``None`` for the dummy root and for an assistant leaf we generated but
49	    whose ``response_message`` was empty).
50	
51	    The two kinds are distinguished by whether ``turn`` is set, which reflects
52	    WHERE the message came from:
53	
54	    * **generated** (``turn is not None``): an assistant message the model
55	      actually generated this turn, fed in via ``record_turn``. ``turn`` holds
56	      its :class:`TurnRecord` -- the prompt/output ids, logprobs and finish
57	      reason that ``get_trajectory`` linearizes into training tokens.
58	    * **routing-only** (``turn is None``): the message came from the prompt, not
59	      from generation, so it only exists to route. This is every
60	      system/user/tool node, AND any assistant we did NOT generate: a foreign
61	      assistant the client replayed in a later prompt, or a prior generated turn
62	      demoted by the rewrite-merge in ``_try_merge_assistant_rewrite``.
63	    """
64	
65	    def __init__(
66	        self,
67	        *,
68	        role: str | None = None,
69	        message: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
70	        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
71	        parent: MessageNode | None = None,
72	    ) -> None:
73	        self.role = role
74	        self.message = message
75	        self.metadata = dict(metadata or {})
76	        self.parent: MessageNode | None = parent
77	        self.children: list[MessageNode] = []
78	        self.turn: TurnRecord | None = None  # the generated TurnRecord, else None (routing-only)
79	        self.turn_index: int | None = None
80	        # Shared by sibling leaf paths; the first to reach it trains on it, the rest
81	        # re-emit it as loss_mask=0 context -- so each response is trained exactly once.
82	        self.response_trained: bool = False
83	
84	    @property
85	    def is_root(self) -> bool:
86	        return self.parent is None
87	
88	    def add_child(self, child: MessageNode) -> MessageNode:
89	        child.parent = self
90	        self.children.append(child)
91	        return child
92	
93	    def path_from_root(self) -> list[MessageNode]:
94	        """Ordered list of nodes from the first non-root ancestor down to self."""
95	        chain: list[MessageNode] = []
96	        node: MessageNode | None = self
97	        while node is not None and not node.is_root:
98	            chain.append(node)
99	            node = node.parent
100	        chain.reverse()
101	        return chain
102	
103	    def leaves(self) -> Iterator[MessageNode]:
104	        if not self.children:
105	            yield self
106	            return
107	        for c in self.children:
108	            yield from c.leaves()
109	
110	
111	# ===========================================================================
112	# drift classification — how an incoming turn's prompt relates to held tokens
113	# ===========================================================================
114	
115	
116	def _common_prefix_len(a: list[int], b: list[int], chunk: int = 4096) -> int:
117	    limit = min(len(a), len(b))
118	    matched = 0
119	    while matched < limit:
120	        chunk_end = min(matched + chunk, limit)
121	        if a[matched:chunk_end] == b[matched:chunk_end]:
122	            matched = chunk_end
123	        else:
124	            while matched < chunk_end and a[matched] == b[matched]:
125	                matched += 1
126	            return matched
127	    return matched
128	
129	
130	class DriftKind(enum.Enum):
131	    CLEAN = "clean"  # drift == 0: prompt_ids exactly extends held tokens; append the tail beyond them
132	    REALIGN = "realign"  # drift inside the most-recent response span and short incoming response; replace that span (loss_mask=0)
133	    FORK = "fork"  # everything else: close this builder, open a fresh one as a fork
134	
135	
136	# ===========================================================================
137	# SampleBuilder — accumulates turns into one trainable Sample (fork closes it)
138	# ===========================================================================
139	
140	
141	class _SampleBuilder:
142	    """Accumulates a chain's turns into the token sequence of one ``Sample``.
143	
144	    A chain of turns is appended one at a time via :meth:`append_turn`. Ideally
145	    each turn's prompt exactly extends the tokens we already hold, but a replayed
146	    turn rarely re-tokenizes byte-for-byte: TITO round-trips and chat-template
147	    re-rendering both perturb the ids of content we've already seen. The builder
148	    handles this drift in a source-agnostic way, classified by where and how far
149	    the prompt diverges from the held tokens (see :meth:`classify_token_drift`):
150	
151	    * **CLEAN** -- no drift; append the prompt tail beyond what we hold.
152	    * **REALIGN** -- a short divergence inside the most-recent response span;
153	      overwrite that span from the prompt as loss_mask=0 and keep accumulating.
154	    * **FORK** -- divergence too large or too early to absorb; this builder is
155	      rejected and the caller closes it and opens a fresh one. That boundary is
156	      the "fork".
157	
158	    Each surviving builder yields one Sample.
159	    """
160	
161	    def __init__(self, fork_threshold: int) -> None:
162	        self._fork_threshold = fork_threshold
163	        self.tokens: list[int] = []
164	        self.loss_mask: list[int] = []
165	        self.logprobs: list[float] = []
166	        self.last_response_start_idx: int | None = None
167	        self.leading_prompt_len: int = 0
168	
169	    def classify_token_drift(self, turn: TurnRecord) -> DriftKind:
170	        """Decide how this builder should absorb ``turn``'s prompt.
171	
172	        The incoming turn's prompt is expected to match the tokens this builder
173	        already holds as an exact prefix. When token drift has occurred -- the
174	        prompt diverges from the held tokens -- we decide whether to REALIGN
175	        (heal a short divergence inside the most-recent response span) or to FORK
176	        (``len(turn.output_ids) >= fork_threshold``, or the divergence sits too
177	        early to absorb). With no drift the turn is handled the CLEAN way -- a
178	        plain prefix extension.
179	        """
180	        realign_at = _common_prefix_len(self.tokens, turn.prompt_ids)
181	        drift = len(self.tokens) - realign_at
182	
183	        if drift == 0:
184	            return DriftKind.CLEAN
185	
186	        # REALIGN only heals drift that falls inside the most-recent response span
187	        # (and is short); divergence anywhere earlier, or an empty builder, forks.
188	        start = self.last_response_start_idx
189	        if start is not None and realign_at >= start and len(turn.output_ids) < self._fork_threshold:
190	            return DriftKind.REALIGN
191	        return DriftKind.FORK
192	
193	    def append_turn(self, turn: TurnRecord, kind: DriftKind, *, trained: bool = True) -> None:
194	        """Append one turn into this SampleBuilder, branching on ``kind``: for REALIGN
195	        we overwrite the already-saved response span, for CLEAN we just append this
196	        turn's prompt tail."""
197	        assert kind is not DriftKind.FORK, "append_turn called on a builder that would fork"
198	
199	        is_first_turn = self.last_response_start_idx is None
200	
201	        # --- append this turn's prompt tail (loss_mask=0) ---
202	        if kind is DriftKind.REALIGN:
203	            self._align_to_prompt(turn.prompt_ids)  # drop the drifted tail, re-append from prompt
204	        else:  # CLEAN: held tokens are an exact prefix of prompt_ids; append the tail beyond them
205	            self._append_tokens(turn.prompt_ids[len(self.tokens) :], loss_mask=0)
206	
207	        # --- append this turn's generated response (loss_mask=1 unless re-emitted as context) ---
208	        self.last_response_start_idx = len(self.tokens)
209	        self._append_tokens(
210	            turn.output_ids, loss_mask=int(trained), logprobs=turn.output_log_probs if trained else None
211	        )
212	
213	        if is_first_turn:
214	            self.leading_prompt_len = len(turn.prompt_ids)
215	
216	    def _align_to_prompt(self, prompt_ids: list[int]) -> None:
217	        """Heal REALIGN drift by overwriting the most-recent response span with
218	        ``prompt_ids`` as loss_mask=0: the drifted tokens carry no signal, and re-appending
219	        from the prompt keeps the builder contiguous. Earlier turns are untouched."""
220	        response_start = self.last_response_start_idx
221	        tail = prompt_ids[response_start:]
222	        self.tokens[response_start:] = tail
223	        self.loss_mask[response_start:] = [0] * len(tail)
224	        self.logprobs[response_start:] = [0.0] * len(tail)
225	
226	    def _append_tokens(self, ids: list[int], *, loss_mask: int, logprobs: list[float] | None = None) -> None:
227	        self.tokens.extend(ids)
228	        self.loss_mask.extend([loss_mask] * len(ids))
229	        self.logprobs.extend(logprobs if logprobs else [0.0] * len(ids))
230	
231	    def has_trained_response(self) -> bool:
232	        return any(self.loss_mask[self.leading_prompt_len :])
233	
234	    def to_sample(
235	        self, base_sample: Sample, extra_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None, max_sample_tokens: int = 0
236	    ) -> Sample:
237	        """Emit the accumulated tokens as one ``Sample``, stripping the first-turn
238	        prompt so loss_mask / logprobs cover only the response region."""
239	        start = self.leading_prompt_len  # first-turn prompt stripped; response region starts here
240	        tokens = list(self.tokens)
241	        loss_mask = self.loss_mask
242	        logprobs = self.logprobs
243	        if max_sample_tokens and len(tokens) > max_sample_tokens:
244	            tokens = tokens[:max_sample_tokens]
245	            loss_mask = loss_mask[:max_sample_tokens]
246	            logprobs = logprobs[:max_sample_tokens]
247	        md = dict(extra_metadata or {})
248	        return Sample(
249	            index=base_sample.index,
250	            group_index=base_sample.group_index,
251	            rollout_id=base_sample.rollout_id if base_sample.rollout_id is not None else base_sample.index,
252	            prompt=base_sample.prompt,
253	            label=base_sample.label,
254	            tokens=tokens,
255	            response_length=len(loss_mask) - start,
256	            loss_mask=loss_mask[start:],
257	            rollout_log_probs=logprobs[start:],
258	            reward=0.0,
259	            status=Sample.Status.COMPLETED,
260	            metadata=md,
261	        )
262	
263	
264	# ===========================================================================
265	# TrajectoryManager
266	# ===========================================================================
267	
268	
269	class TrajectoryManager:
270	    def __init__(self, *, fork_threshold_tokens: int | None = None) -> None:
271	        self._fork_threshold: int = 1024 if fork_threshold_tokens is None else fork_threshold_tokens
272	        self._trees: dict[str, MessageNode] = {}
273	        self._turn_count: dict[str, int] = {}
274	
275	    # -------------------- public ------------------------------------------
276	
277	    def has_session(self, sid: str) -> bool:
278	        return sid in self._trees
279	
280	    def turn_count(self, sid: str) -> int:
281	        return self._turn_count.get(sid, 0)
282	
283	    def record_turn(
284	        self,
285	        sid: str,
286	        *,
287	        turn: TurnRecord,
288	        prompt_messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
289	        response_message: dict[str, Any] | None,
290	        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
291	    ) -> None:
292	        if not prompt_messages:
293	            logger.warning("record_turn(sid=%s): empty prompt_messages; skipping", sid)
294	            return
295	        assert not turn.output_log_probs or len(turn.output_log_probs) == len(turn.output_ids), (
296	            f"turn.output_log_probs length {len(turn.output_log_probs)} != "
297	            f"turn.output_ids length {len(turn.output_ids)}"
298	        )
299	
300	        root = self._trees.setdefault(sid, MessageNode())
301	
302	        node, depth = self._find_mount_point(root, prompt_messages)
303	        node, depth = self._try_merge_assistant_rewrite(sid, node, prompt_messages, depth)
304	        node = self._mount_prompt_messages(node, prompt_messages[depth:])
305	        self._attach_assistant_leaf(sid, node, turn=turn, response_message=response_message, metadata=metadata)
306	
307	    def get_trajectory(
308	        self,
309	        sid: str,
310	        *,
311	        base_sample: Sample,
312	        reward: float = 0.0,
313	        extra_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
314	        max_sample_tokens: int = 0,
315	    ) -> list[Sample]:
316	        """Linearize this sid's routing tree into slime ``Sample`` objects and
317	        consume the session.
318	
319	        Each routing leaf yields one or more Samples; ``reward`` is assigned in
320	        full to every emitted Sample (not split across them), so each trained
321	        turn carries the trajectory's outcome reward. The sid is dropped
322	        afterwards, so a second call for the same sid returns ``[]``.
323	        """
324	        root = self._trees.get(sid)
325	        if root is None:
326	            return []
327	
328	        samples: list[Sample] = []
329	        for routing_leaf in root.leaves():
330	            if routing_leaf.is_root:
331	                continue
332	            chain = routing_leaf.path_from_root()
333	            samples.extend(
334	                self._chain_to_samples(
335	                    chain, base_sample=base_sample, extra_metadata=extra_metadata, max_sample_tokens=max_sample_tokens
336	                )
337	            )
338	
339	        for s in samples:
340	            s.reward = reward
341	
342	        self._trees.pop(sid, None)
343	        self._turn_count.pop(sid, None)
344	        return samples
345	
346	    def drop_session(self, sid: str) -> None:
347	        self._trees.pop(sid, None)
348	        self._turn_count.pop(sid, None)
349	
350	    # -------------------- internals ----------------------------------------
351	
352	    def _find_mount_point(self, root: MessageNode, messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[MessageNode, int]:
353	        """Walk down the tree matching each message by role and dict equality (==),
354	        returning the deepest node that still matches and where to mount the rest."""
355	        node = root
356	        depth = 0
357	        while depth < len(messages):
358	            msg = messages[depth]
359	            next_child = None
360	            for child in node.children:
361	                if child.role == msg.get("role") and child.message == msg:
362	                    next_child = child
363	                    break
364	            if next_child is None:
365	                break
366	            node = next_child
367	            depth += 1
368	        return node, depth
369	
370	    def _try_merge_assistant_rewrite(
371	        self,
372	        sid: str,
373	        node: MessageNode,
374	        prompt_messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
375	        depth: int,
376	    ) -> tuple[MessageNode, int]:
377	        """Merge a short assistant-rewrite onto its node instead of forking.
378	
379	        A harness may replay a prior assistant message slightly re-rendered (e.g.
380	        whitespace) in a later prompt. It no longer matches the node we generated,
381	        so it would fork -- stranding the original generated turn as a dead-end
382	        leaf that still emits its own training Sample. Instead we overwrite that
383	        node's message in place and stop training its generated content (demote to
384	        routing-only), so only the live branch trains. This only applies below
385	        ``fork_threshold``: a long abandoned response carries enough real signal
386	        to fork and train standalone.
387	
388	        Forking is always safe (a rewrite mounts as routing-only); this is purely
389	        a cleanup. So we merge only when the mount point has exactly one assistant
390	        child that is a leaf, generated (``turn`` set), and short (response <
391	        ``fork_threshold``), and fork otherwise, since absorbing destroys a
392	        generated TurnRecord irreversibly.
393	        """
394	        if self._fork_threshold <= 0:
395	            return node, depth  # feature off
396	        if depth >= len(prompt_messages) or prompt_messages[depth].get("role") != "assistant":
397	            return node, depth  # genuine non-assistant history fork -> leave it
398	
399	        asst_children = [c for c in node.children if c.role == "assistant"]
400	        if len(asst_children) != 1:
401	            if len(asst_children) > 1:
402	                logger.warning(
403	                    "record_turn(sid=%s turn=%s): %d assistant children at mount "
404	                    "point; can't tell which the rewrite targets, so forking.",
405	                    sid,
406	                    self._turn_count.get(sid, 0) + 1,
407	                    len(asst_children),
408	                )
409	            return node, depth
410	
411	        rewritten_node = asst_children[0]
412	        if (
413	            rewritten_node.children
414	            or rewritten_node.turn is None
415	            or len(rewritten_node.turn.output_ids) >= self._fork_threshold
416	        ):
417	            return node, depth
418	
419	        rewritten_node.metadata["merged_rewrite"] = {
420	            "abandoned_turn_index": rewritten_node.turn_index,
421	            "abandoned_response_tokens": len(rewritten_node.turn.output_ids),
422	        }
423	        rewritten_node.turn = None
424	        rewritten_node.turn_index = None
425	        rewritten_node.message = prompt_messages[depth]
426	        return rewritten_node, depth + 1
427	
428	    def _mount_prompt_messages(
429	        self,
430	        node: MessageNode,
431	        remaining_messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
432	    ) -> MessageNode:
433	        for m in remaining_messages:
434	            node = node.add_child(MessageNode(role=m.get("role"), message=m))
435	        return node
436	
437	    def _attach_assistant_leaf(
438	        self,
439	        sid: str,
440	        node: MessageNode,
441	        *,
442	        turn: TurnRecord,
443	        response_message: dict[str, Any] | None,
444	        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None,
445	    ) -> None:
446	        asst = MessageNode(
447	            role="assistant",
448	            message=response_message,
449	            metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
450	        )
451	        asst.turn = turn
452	        asst.turn_index = self._turn_count.get(sid, 0) + 1
453	        node.add_child(asst)
454	        self._turn_count[sid] = asst.turn_index
455	
456	    def _split_chain_into_builders(self, chain: list[MessageNode]) -> list[_SampleBuilder]:
457	        """Pack the chain's generated turns into per-Sample token builders.
458	
459	        Turns flow into the current builder until one can't extend it as an
460	        exact prefix (re-tokenization drift past what we can drop); that turn
461	        opens a new builder -- a fork. A generated turn shared by sibling leaves
462	        is trained only on the first leaf to claim it; later leaves re-emit it
463	        as loss_mask=0 context so the shared prefix isn't double-counted.
464	        """
465	        asst_nodes = [n for n in chain if n.role == "assistant" and n.turn is not None]
466	
467	        builders: list[_SampleBuilder] = []
468	        for asst_node in asst_nodes:
469	            trained = not asst_node.response_trained
470	            asst_node.response_trained = True
471	
472	            if not builders or (kind := builders[-1].classify_token_drift(asst_node.turn)) is DriftKind.FORK:
473	                builders.append(_SampleBuilder(self._fork_threshold))
474	                builders[-1].append_turn(asst_node.turn, DriftKind.CLEAN, trained=trained)
475	            else:
476	                builders[-1].append_turn(asst_node.turn, kind, trained=trained)
477	        return builders
478	
479	    def _chain_to_samples(
480	        self,
481	        chain: list[MessageNode],
482	        *,
483	        base_sample: Sample,
484	        extra_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None,
485	        max_sample_tokens: int = 0,
486	    ) -> list[Sample]:
487	
488	        asst_nodes = [n for n in chain if n.role == "assistant" and n.turn is not None]
489	        truncated = bool(asst_nodes) and asst_nodes[-1].turn.finish_reason == "length"
490	        use_tool = any(bool((n.message or {}).get("tool_calls")) for n in asst_nodes)
491	        ill_formed = any(n.turn.ill_formed for n in asst_nodes)
492	        md = {
493	            **(extra_metadata or {}),
494	            "truncated": truncated,
495	            "use_tool": use_tool,
496	            "ill_formed": ill_formed,
497	        }
498	        return [

"""Build a per-session training trajectory from multi-turn conversation data.

The :class:`TrajectoryManager` builds one trajectory per session. ``record_turn``
feeds in each turn (prompt messages + the served model's sglang snapshot),
routing it into a per-sid message tree; ``get_trajectory`` then linearizes that
tree into a ``list[Sample]`` of loss-masked training rows, tolerating TITO
re-tokenization drift via fork/replace.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import enum
import logging
from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Any

from slime.utils.types import Sample

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ===========================================================================
# TurnRecord
# ===========================================================================


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class TurnRecord:
    """One sglang ``/generate`` snapshot: the contract between an adapter and the
    manager. Adapters build it from a turn's prompt/output token ids; ``record_turn``
    consumes it."""

    prompt_ids: list[int]
    output_ids: list[int]
    finish_reason: str
    output_log_probs: list[float] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
    ill_formed: bool = False


# ===========================================================================
# MessageNode
# ===========================================================================


class MessageNode:
    """One node in a session's routing tree, carrying a single chat message
    (``None`` for the dummy root and for an assistant leaf we generated but
    whose ``response_message`` was empty).

    The two kinds are distinguished by whether ``turn`` is set, which reflects
    WHERE the message came from:

    * **generated** (``turn is not None``): an assistant message the model
      actually generated this turn, fed in via ``record_turn``. ``turn`` holds
      its :class:`TurnRecord` -- the prompt/output ids, logprobs and finish
      reason that ``get_trajectory`` linearizes into training tokens.
    * **routing-only** (``turn is None``): the message came from the prompt, not
      from generation, so it only exists to route. This is every
      system/user/tool node, AND any assistant we did NOT generate: a foreign
      assistant the client replayed in a later prompt, or a prior generated turn
      demoted by the rewrite-merge in ``_try_merge_assistant_rewrite``.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        role: str | None = None,
        message: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        parent: MessageNode | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.role = role
        self.message = message
        self.metadata = dict(metadata or {})
        self.parent: MessageNode | None = parent
        self.children: list[MessageNode] = []
        self.turn: TurnRecord | None = None  # the generated TurnRecord, else None (routing-only)
        self.turn_index: int | None = None
        # Shared by sibling leaf paths; the first to reach it trains on it, the rest
        # re-emit it as loss_mask=0 context -- so each response is trained exactly once.
        self.response_trained: bool = False

    @property
    def is_root(self) -> bool:
        return self.parent is None

    def add_child(self, child: MessageNode) -> MessageNode:
        child.parent = self
        self.children.append(child)
        return child

    def path_from_root(self) -> list[MessageNode]:
        """Ordered list of nodes from the first non-root ancestor down to self."""
        chain: list[MessageNode] = []
        node: MessageNode | None = self
        while node is not None and not node.is_root:
            chain.append(node)
            node = node.parent
        chain.reverse()
        return chain

    def leaves(self) -> Iterator[MessageNode]:
        if not self.children:
            yield self
            return
        for c in self.children:
            yield from c.leaves()


# ===========================================================================
# drift classification — how an incoming turn's prompt relates to held tokens
# ===========================================================================


def _common_prefix_len(a: list[int], b: list[int], chunk: int = 4096) -> int:
    limit = min(len(a), len(b))
    matched = 0
    while matched < limit:
        chunk_end = min(matched + chunk, limit)
        if a[matched:chunk_end] == b[matched:chunk_end]:
            matched = chunk_end
        else:
            while matched < chunk_end and a[matched] == b[matched]:
                matched += 1
            return matched
    return matched


class DriftKind(enum.Enum):
    CLEAN = "clean"  # drift == 0: prompt_ids exactly extends held tokens; append the tail beyond them
    REALIGN = "realign"  # drift inside the most-recent response span and short incoming response; replace that span (loss_mask=0)
    FORK = "fork"  # everything else: close this builder, open a fresh one as a fork


# ===========================================================================
# SampleBuilder — accumulates turns into one trainable Sample (fork closes it)
# ===========================================================================


class _SampleBuilder:
    """Accumulates a chain's turns into the token sequence of one ``Sample``.

    A chain of turns is appended one at a time via :meth:`append_turn`. Ideally
    each turn's prompt exactly extends the tokens we already hold, but a replayed
    turn rarely re-tokenizes byte-for-byte: TITO round-trips and chat-template
    re-rendering both perturb the ids of content we've already seen. The builder
    handles this drift in a source-agnostic way, classified by where and how far
    the prompt diverges from the held tokens (see :meth:`classify_token_drift`):

    * **CLEAN** -- no drift; append the prompt tail beyond what we hold.
    * **REALIGN** -- a short divergence inside the most-recent response span;
      overwrite that span from the prompt as loss_mask=0 and keep accumulating.
    * **FORK** -- divergence too large or too early to absorb; this builder is
      rejected and the caller closes it and opens a fresh one. That boundary is
      the "fork".

    Each surviving builder yields one Sample.
    """

    def __init__(self, fork_threshold: int) -> None:
        self._fork_threshold = fork_threshold
        self.tokens: list[int] = []
        self.loss_mask: list[int] = []
        self.logprobs: list[float] = []
        self.last_response_start_idx: int | None = None
        self.leading_prompt_len: int = 0

    def classify_token_drift(self, turn: TurnRecord) -> DriftKind:
        """Decide how this builder should absorb ``turn``'s prompt.

        The incoming turn's prompt is expected to match the tokens this builder
        already holds as an exact prefix. When token drift has occurred -- the
        prompt diverges from the held tokens -- we decide whether to REALIGN
        (heal a short divergence inside the most-recent response span) or to FORK
        (``len(turn.output_ids) >= fork_threshold``, or the divergence sits too
        early to absorb). With no drift the turn is handled the CLEAN way -- a
        plain prefix extension.
        """
        realign_at = _common_prefix_len(self.tokens, turn.prompt_ids)
        drift = len(self.tokens) - realign_at

        if drift == 0:
            return DriftKind.CLEAN

        # REALIGN only heals drift that falls inside the most-recent response span
        # (and is short); divergence anywhere earlier, or an empty builder, forks.
        start = self.last_response_start_idx
        if start is not None and realign_at >= start and len(turn.output_ids) < self._fork_threshold:
            return DriftKind.REALIGN
        return DriftKind.FORK

    def append_turn(self, turn: TurnRecord, kind: DriftKind, *, trained: bool = True) -> None:
        """Append one turn into this SampleBuilder, branching on ``kind``: for REALIGN
        we overwrite the already-saved response span, for CLEAN we just append this
        turn's prompt tail."""
        assert kind is not DriftKind.FORK, "append_turn called on a builder that would fork"

        is_first_turn = self.last_response_start_idx is None

        # --- append this turn's prompt tail (loss_mask=0) ---
        if kind is DriftKind.REALIGN:
            self._align_to_prompt(turn.prompt_ids)  # drop the drifted tail, re-append from prompt
        else:  # CLEAN: held tokens are an exact prefix of prompt_ids; append the tail beyond them
            self._append_tokens(turn.prompt_ids[len(self.tokens) :], loss_mask=0)

        # --- append this turn's generated response (loss_mask=1 unless re-emitted as context) ---
        self.last_response_start_idx = len(self.tokens)
        self._append_tokens(
            turn.output_ids, loss_mask=int(trained), logprobs=turn.output_log_probs if trained else None
        )

        if is_first_turn:
            self.leading_prompt_len = len(turn.prompt_ids)

    def _align_to_prompt(self, prompt_ids: list[int]) -> None:
        """Heal REALIGN drift by overwriting the most-recent response span with
        ``prompt_ids`` as loss_mask=0: the drifted tokens carry no signal, and re-appending
        from the prompt keeps the builder contiguous. Earlier turns are untouched."""
        response_start = self.last_response_start_idx
        tail = prompt_ids[response_start:]
        self.tokens[response_start:] = tail
        self.loss_mask[response_start:] = [0] * len(tail)
        self.logprobs[response_start:] = [0.0] * len(tail)

    def _append_tokens(self, ids: list[int], *, loss_mask: int, logprobs: list[float] | None = None) -> None:
        self.tokens.extend(ids)
        self.loss_mask.extend([loss_mask] * len(ids))
        self.logprobs.extend(logprobs if logprobs else [0.0] * len(ids))

    def has_trained_response(self) -> bool:
        return any(self.loss_mask[self.leading_prompt_len :])

    def to_sample(
        self, base_sample: Sample, extra_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None, max_sample_tokens: int = 0
    ) -> Sample:
        """Emit the accumulated tokens as one ``Sample``, stripping the first-turn
        prompt so loss_mask / logprobs cover only the response region."""
        start = self.leading_prompt_len  # first-turn prompt stripped; response region starts here
        tokens = list(self.tokens)
        loss_mask = self.loss_mask
        logprobs = self.logprobs
        if max_sample_tokens and len(tokens) > max_sample_tokens:
            tokens = tokens[:max_sample_tokens]
            loss_mask = loss_mask[:max_sample_tokens]
            logprobs = logprobs[:max_sample_tokens]
        md = dict(extra_metadata or {})
        return Sample(
            index=base_sample.index,
            group_index=base_sample.group_index,
            rollout_id=base_sample.rollout_id if base_sample.rollout_id is not None else base_sample.index,
            prompt=base_sample.prompt,
            label=base_sample.label,
            tokens=tokens,
            response_length=len(loss_mask) - start,
            loss_mask=loss_mask[start:],
            rollout_log_probs=logprobs[start:],
            reward=0.0,
            status=Sample.Status.COMPLETED,
            metadata=md,
        )


# ===========================================================================
# TrajectoryManager
# ===========================================================================


class TrajectoryManager:
    def __init__(self, *, fork_threshold_tokens: int | None = None) -> None:
        self._fork_threshold: int = 1024 if fork_threshold_tokens is None else fork_threshold_tokens
        self._trees: dict[str, MessageNode] = {}
        self._turn_count: dict[str, int] = {}

    # -------------------- public ------------------------------------------

    def has_session(self, sid: str) -> bool:
        return sid in self._trees

    def turn_count(self, sid: str) -> int:
        return self._turn_count.get(sid, 0)

    def record_turn(
        self,
        sid: str,
        *,
        turn: TurnRecord,
        prompt_messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
        response_message: dict[str, Any] | None,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not prompt_messages:
            logger.warning("record_turn(sid=%s): empty prompt_messages; skipping", sid)
            return
        assert not turn.output_log_probs or len(turn.output_log_probs) == len(turn.output_ids), (
            f"turn.output_log_probs length {len(turn.output_log_probs)} != "
            f"turn.output_ids length {len(turn.output_ids)}"
        )

        root = self._trees.setdefault(sid, MessageNode())

        node, depth = self._find_mount_point(root, prompt_messages)
        node, depth = self._try_merge_assistant_rewrite(sid, node, prompt_messages, depth)
        node = self._mount_prompt_messages(node, prompt_messages[depth:])
        self._attach_assistant_leaf(sid, node, turn=turn, response_message=response_message, metadata=metadata)

    def get_trajectory(
        self,
        sid: str,
        *,
        base_sample: Sample,
        reward: float = 0.0,
        extra_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        max_sample_tokens: int = 0,
    ) -> list[Sample]:
        """Linearize this sid's routing tree into slime ``Sample`` objects and
        consume the session.

        Each routing leaf yields one or more Samples; ``reward`` is assigned in
        full to every emitted Sample (not split across them), so each trained
        turn carries the trajectory's outcome reward. The sid is dropped
        afterwards, so a second call for the same sid returns ``[]``.
        """
        root = self._trees.get(sid)
        if root is None:
            return []

        samples: list[Sample] = []
        for routing_leaf in root.leaves():
            if routing_leaf.is_root:
                continue
            chain = routing_leaf.path_from_root()
            samples.extend(
                self._chain_to_samples(
                    chain, base_sample=base_sample, extra_metadata=extra_metadata, max_sample_tokens=max_sample_tokens
                )
            )

        for s in samples:
            s.reward = reward

        self._trees.pop(sid, None)
        self._turn_count.pop(sid, None)
        return samples

    def drop_session(self, sid: str) -> None:
        self._trees.pop(sid, None)
        self._turn_count.pop(sid, None)

    # -------------------- internals ----------------------------------------

    def _find_mount_point(self, root: MessageNode, messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[MessageNode, int]:
        """Walk down the tree matching each message by role and dict equality (==),
        returning the deepest node that still matches and where to mount the rest."""
        node = root
        depth = 0
        while depth < len(messages):
            msg = messages[depth]
            next_child = None
            for child in node.children:
                if child.role == msg.get("role") and child.message == msg:
                    next_child = child
                    break
            if next_child is None:
                break
            node = next_child
            depth += 1
        return node, depth

    def _try_merge_assistant_rewrite(
        self,
        sid: str,
        node: MessageNode,
        prompt_messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
        depth: int,
    ) -> tuple[MessageNode, int]:
        """Merge a short assistant-rewrite onto its node instead of forking.

        A harness may replay a prior assistant message slightly re-rendered (e.g.
        whitespace) in a later prompt. It no longer matches the node we generated,
        so it would fork -- stranding the original generated turn as a dead-end
        leaf that still emits its own training Sample. Instead we overwrite that
        node's message in place and stop training its generated content (demote to
        routing-only), so only the live branch trains. This only applies below
        ``fork_threshold``: a long abandoned response carries enough real signal
        to fork and train standalone.

        Forking is always safe (a rewrite mounts as routing-only); this is purely
        a cleanup. So we merge only when the mount point has exactly one assistant
        child that is a leaf, generated (``turn`` set), and short (response <
        ``fork_threshold``), and fork otherwise, since absorbing destroys a
        generated TurnRecord irreversibly.
        """
        if self._fork_threshold <= 0:
            return node, depth  # feature off
        if depth >= len(prompt_messages) or prompt_messages[depth].get("role") != "assistant":
            return node, depth  # genuine non-assistant history fork -> leave it

        asst_children = [c for c in node.children if c.role == "assistant"]
        if len(asst_children) != 1:
            if len(asst_children) > 1:
                logger.warning(
                    "record_turn(sid=%s turn=%s): %d assistant children at mount "
                    "point; can't tell which the rewrite targets, so forking.",
                    sid,
                    self._turn_count.get(sid, 0) + 1,
                    len(asst_children),
                )
            return node, depth

        rewritten_node = asst_children[0]
        if (
            rewritten_node.children
            or rewritten_node.turn is None
            or len(rewritten_node.turn.output_ids) >= self._fork_threshold
        ):
            return node, depth

        rewritten_node.metadata["merged_rewrite"] = {
            "abandoned_turn_index": rewritten_node.turn_index,
            "abandoned_response_tokens": len(rewritten_node.turn.output_ids),
        }
        rewritten_node.turn = None
        rewritten_node.turn_index = None
        rewritten_node.message = prompt_messages[depth]
        return rewritten_node, depth + 1

    def _mount_prompt_messages(
        self,
        node: MessageNode,
        remaining_messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> MessageNode:
        for m in remaining_messages:
            node = node.add_child(MessageNode(role=m.get("role"), message=m))
        return node

    def _attach_assistant_leaf(
        self,
        sid: str,
        node: MessageNode,
        *,
        turn: TurnRecord,
        response_message: dict[str, Any] | None,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None,
    ) -> None:
        asst = MessageNode(
            role="assistant",
            message=response_message,
            metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
        )
        asst.turn = turn
        asst.turn_index = self._turn_count.get(sid, 0) + 1
        node.add_child(asst)
        self._turn_count[sid] = asst.turn_index

    def _split_chain_into_builders(self, chain: list[MessageNode]) -> list[_SampleBuilder]:
        """Pack the chain's generated turns into per-Sample token builders.

        Turns flow into the current builder until one can't extend it as an
        exact prefix (re-tokenization drift past what we can drop); that turn
        opens a new builder -- a fork. A generated turn shared by sibling leaves
        is trained only on the first leaf to claim it; later leaves re-emit it
        as loss_mask=0 context so the shared prefix isn't double-counted.
        """
        asst_nodes = [n for n in chain if n.role == "assistant" and n.turn is not None]

        builders: list[_SampleBuilder] = []
        for asst_node in asst_nodes:
            trained = not asst_node.response_trained
            asst_node.response_trained = True

            if not builders or (kind := builders[-1].classify_token_drift(asst_node.turn)) is DriftKind.FORK:
                builders.append(_SampleBuilder(self._fork_threshold))
                builders[-1].append_turn(asst_node.turn, DriftKind.CLEAN, trained=trained)
            else:
                builders[-1].append_turn(asst_node.turn, kind, trained=trained)
        return builders

    def _chain_to_samples(
        self,
        chain: list[MessageNode],
        *,
        base_sample: Sample,
        extra_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None,
        max_sample_tokens: int = 0,
    ) -> list[Sample]:

        asst_nodes = [n for n in chain if n.role == "assistant" and n.turn is not None]
        truncated = bool(asst_nodes) and asst_nodes[-1].turn.finish_reason == "length"
        use_tool = any(bool((n.message or {}).get("tool_calls")) for n in asst_nodes)
        ill_formed = any(n.turn.ill_formed for n in asst_nodes)
        md = {
            **(extra_metadata or {}),
            "truncated": truncated,
            "use_tool": use_tool,
            "ill_formed": ill_formed,
        }
        return [
            builder.to_sample(base_sample, md, max_sample_tokens)
            for builder in self._split_chain_into_builders(chain)
            if builder.has_trained_response()
        ]


__all__ = [
    "TrajectoryManager",
    "TurnRecord",
]

"""Model-output parsing helpers for agent harnesses."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import re
from typing import Any


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class ParsedModelOutput:
    """Structured view of one decoded model output."""

    reasoning: str
    text: str
    tool_uses: list[dict[str, Any]]
    ill_formed: bool = False


def parse_model_output(
    raw_output: str,
    *,
    tools_schema: list[dict] | None,
    tool_parser_name: str | None,
    reasoning_parser_name: str | None,
) -> ParsedModelOutput:
    """Parse raw model text into reasoning, visible text, and tool uses.

    The heavy format-specific work is delegated to SGLang's reasoning and
    function-call parsers. The XML fallback covers Anthropic-style tool-call
    text that some coding-agent models still emit occasionally.
    """
    reasoning, body_text = "", raw_output
    if reasoning_parser_name:
        from sglang.srt.parser.reasoning_parser import ReasoningParser

        r, b = ReasoningParser(
            model_type=reasoning_parser_name,
            stream_reasoning=False,
        ).parse_non_stream(raw_output)
        reasoning, body_text = r or "", b or ""
        if not reasoning and "</think>" in body_text:
            reasoning, body_text = body_text.split("</think>", 1)

    body_text, tool_uses, ill_formed = parse_tool_uses(body_text, tools_schema, tool_parser_name)
    return ParsedModelOutput(
        reasoning=reasoning,
        text=(body_text or "").strip(),
        tool_uses=tool_uses,
        ill_formed=ill_formed,
    )


def parse_tool_uses(
    body_text: str,
    tools_schema: list[dict] | None,
    tool_parser_name: str | None,
) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]], bool]:
    """Parse tool calls from body text and return visible text plus tool uses."""
    tool_uses: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    ill_formed = False
    if tool_parser_name and tools_schema:
        from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
        from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser

        sg_tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(**d["function"])) for d in tools_schema]
        parser = FunctionCallParser(tools=sg_tools, tool_call_parser=tool_parser_name)
        calls = []
        if parser.has_tool_call(body_text):
            try:
                body_text, calls = parser.parse_non_stream(body_text)
            except Exception:
                logger.exception("[agent.parsing] sglang tool-call parsing failed; falling back")
        for c in calls:
            try:
                args = json.loads(c.parameters or "{}")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                args = {"_raw_arguments": c.parameters}
                ill_formed = True
            tool_uses.append({"name": c.name or "tool", "input": args})

    if not tool_uses and tools_schema:
        body_text, tool_uses = parse_xml_tool_uses(body_text, tools_schema)

    return body_text, tool_uses, ill_formed


def parse_xml_tool_uses(body_text: str, tools_schema: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Fallback parser for Anthropic-style XML tool calls."""
    valid_tools = {t.get("function", {}).get("name") for t in tools_schema}
    tool_uses: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    cleaned_parts: list[str] = []
    last = 0
    for m in re.finditer(
        r"<tool_call>\s*<function=([^>]+)>(.*?)</function>\s*</tool_call>",
        body_text,
        flags=re.DOTALL,
    ):
        name, inner = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        if name in valid_tools:
            args = {
                p.group(1): p.group(2).strip()
                for p in re.finditer(r"<parameter=([^>]+)>(.*?)</parameter>", inner, flags=re.DOTALL)
            }
            tool_uses.append({"name": name, "input": args})
            cleaned_parts.append(body_text[last : m.start()])
            last = m.end()
    cleaned_parts.append(body_text[last:])
    return "".join(cleaned_parts), tool_uses

"""Harness-agnostic coding-agent lifecycle in a sandbox.

A harness is a swappable coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, ...). Each one
installs a CLI, writes its own config, and runs the agent against a prompt. The
shared parts (create the agent user, the run skeleton, the launch-detached-and-
poll transport) live here; adding a CLI-style harness means subclassing
BaseHarness and implementing install_cli, write_config and launch_and_wait.
Two module-level helpers cover the common cases: install_npm_cli for
npm-packaged CLIs, and run_agent for the launch-the-agent-to-completion case.

The base knows nothing about the task: run() takes only generic fields
(workdir / session_id / adapter_url / prompt). Task-specific workspace prep and
scoring live in the example layer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import lzma
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
from abc import ABC, ABCMeta, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from slime.agent import sandbox as _sandbox
from slime.agent.sandbox import Sandbox, exec_and_wait
from slime.utils.misc import SingletonMeta


class SingletonABCMeta(ABCMeta, SingletonMeta):
    pass


# In-sandbox retry budget for the npm global install (transient flakes like
# exit 217). Cheaper than a full sandbox recreate by the caller.
NPM_INSTALL_RETRIES = 3
NPM_INSTALL_BACKOFF_SEC = 2.0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HarnessContext:
    """Generic run context, free of any task fields.

    model_label is the model name the harness advertises to its CLI. The slime
    adapter ignores it and serves whatever upstream sglang has loaded, so it is
    not a run() parameter.
    """

    workdir: str
    session_id: str
    adapter_url: str
    model_label: str = "slime-actor"


class BaseHarness(ABC, metaclass=SingletonABCMeta):
    """Base lifecycle for a sandbox-resident coding agent."""

    # short identifier set by each subclass (claude_code / codex)
    name: str = ""

    @abstractmethod
    async def install_cli(self, sb: Sandbox) -> None:
        """Install the harness CLI into the sandbox.
        npm-packaged harnesses delegate to install_npm_cli."""

    @abstractmethod
    async def write_config(self, sb: Sandbox, ctx: HarnessContext) -> None:
        """Write any CLI config files into the sandbox."""

    @abstractmethod
    async def launch_and_wait(self, sb: Sandbox, ctx: HarnessContext, prompt: str, time_budget_sec: int) -> int:
        """Run the agent to completion and return its exit code.

        A non-interactive CLI builds one shell command and hands it to
        run_agent. An interactive or long-running harness drives its own loop
        here instead.
        """

    async def run(
        self,
        sb: Sandbox,
        *,
        workdir: str,
        session_id: str,
        adapter_url: str,
        time_budget_sec: int,
        prompt: str,
    ) -> int:
        """Run the harness in the sandbox and return its exit code.

        Steps: ensure the agent user -> write config -> launch and wait.
        Workspace prep (writing the problem statement etc.) is the caller's job
        and must run before this.
        """
        await _sandbox.ensure_agent_user(sb, workdir)
        ctx = HarnessContext(
            workdir=workdir,
            session_id=session_id,
            adapter_url=adapter_url,
        )
        await self.write_config(sb, ctx)
        return await self.launch_and_wait(sb, ctx, prompt, time_budget_sec)


async def run_agent(sb: Sandbox, *, workdir: str, start_cmd: str, env: dict[str, str], time_budget_sec: int) -> int:
    """Launch the agent (start_cmd) and run it to completion, returning its exit code."""
    meta_dir = f"{workdir}/.harness"
    await sb.exec(f"mkdir -p {meta_dir} && chown agent:agent {meta_dir}", user="root", check=True, timeout=30)
    exit_code, _ = await exec_and_wait(
        sb,
        cmd=start_cmd,
        user="agent",
        env=env,
        workdir=workdir,
        out_file=f"{meta_dir}/trajectory.jsonl",
        time_budget_sec=time_budget_sec,
        tag="run",
        want_output=False,
    )
    return exit_code


async def install_npm_cli(
    sb: Sandbox,
    *,
    node_runtime: Path,
    npm_package: Path,
    check_cmd: str,
) -> None:
    """Install an npm-packaged CLI into the sandbox: the Node 22 runtime first,
    then the CLI's npm package (global install, then self-check via check_cmd).
    Non-npm harnesses write their own install_cli."""
    await install_node22(sb, node_runtime)

    await sb.write_file("/tmp/harness-cli.tgz", npm_package)
    install_cmd = "npm install -g --prefix=/usr/local --no-audit --no-fund /tmp/harness-cli.tgz && " + check_cmd
    # Detached install with a few in-place retries for transient disk flakes.
    last_log = ""
    for attempt in range(NPM_INSTALL_RETRIES):
        exit_code, last_log = await exec_and_wait(
            sb, cmd=install_cmd, user="root", time_budget_sec=300, tag="harness-npm-install"
        )
        if exit_code == 0:
            return
        if attempt + 1 < NPM_INSTALL_RETRIES:
            await asyncio.sleep(NPM_INSTALL_BACKOFF_SEC * (attempt + 1))
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"npm install failed after {NPM_INSTALL_RETRIES} attempts (exit={exit_code}):\n{last_log[-1000:]}"
    )


async def install_node22(sb: Sandbox, host_tarball: Path) -> None:
    """Install Node 22 over the base image (some base images ship a version too
    old for the CLI). A .xz tarball is decompressed on the host (cached) so
    sandboxes without xz-utils can still run a plain `tar xf`."""
    host_tarball = Path(host_tarball)
    if host_tarball.suffix == ".xz":
        plain = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"coding_agent_rl.{host_tarball.stem}.tar"
        if not plain.exists():
            tmp = plain.with_suffix(".tar.partial")
            with lzma.open(host_tarball, "rb") as src, open(tmp, "wb") as dst:
                shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst)
            os.replace(tmp, plain)
        host_tarball = plain
    await sb.write_file("/tmp/node22.tar", host_tarball)
    await sb.exec(
        "set -e && mkdir -p /opt/node22 && "
        "tar xf /tmp/node22.tar -C /opt/node22 --strip-components=1 && "
        "ln -sf /opt/node22/bin/node /usr/local/bin/node && "
        "ln -sf /opt/node22/bin/npm  /usr/local/bin/npm && "
        "ln -sf /opt/node22/bin/npx  /usr/local/bin/npx && "
        "hash -r 2>/dev/null || true && node --version && npm --version",
        user="root",
        timeout=180,
        check=True,
    )

1	# Agentic RL Training Roadmap
2	
3	slime is not limited to single-turn RL. Its main advantage for agentic training is the combination of high-performance training, SGLang rollout serving, and pluggable data-generation interfaces. This makes it suitable for multi-turn tool use, sandbox interaction, subagent branches, context compaction, and test-based rewards.
4	
5	This page is a roadmap: use it to decide which docs and examples to read when plugging an agent workflow into slime.
6	
7	## Where To Start
8	
9	| Goal | Recommended entry point |
10	| :--- | :--- |
11	| Run a custom agent loop, tool calls, RAG, browser/terminal/sandbox interaction for each sample | [`--custom-generate-function-path`](customization.md#2-custom-generate-function---custom-generate-function-path), [writing a custom generation function](quick_start.md#writing-custom-generation-function) |
12	| Implement verifier rewards, test-based rewards, environment success checks, or an external reward service | [`--custom-rm-path`](customization.md#3-reward-model---custom-rm-path), [writing a custom reward function](quick_start.md#writing-custom-reward-function) |
13	| Return multiple training samples from one prompt, such as subagent, multi-agent, or context-compaction segments | [fan-out return from custom generate](customization.md#returning-multiple-training-samples-for-one-prompt), [`examples/multi_agent`](../_examples_synced/multi_agent/README.md) |
14	| Avoid blocking training on long-tail agent rollouts | [`examples/fully_async`](../_examples_synced/fully_async/README.md) |
15	| Study a full end-to-end agent example with sandboxing, real code edits, and test-based grading | [`examples/coding_agent_rl`](../_examples_synced/coding_agent_rl/README.md) |
16	| Improve SGLang serving throughput for multi-turn agents | [PD Disaggregation](../advanced/pd-disaggregation.md), [SGLang Config](../advanced/sglang-config.md) |
17	| Enable SGLang optimization flags, router policies, or multi-model serving | [How to Use SGLang](usage.md#how-to-use-sglang), [SGLang Config](../advanced/sglang-config.md), [Speculative Decoding](../advanced/speculative-decoding.md), [Low Precision Training](../advanced/low-precision.md) |
18	
19	## Recommended Integration Pattern
20	
21	Most agentic RL tasks should start with `--custom-generate-function-path`. This function converts one agent execution into slime-trainable `Sample` objects: fill `tokens`, `response_length`, `loss_mask`, and `status`, then either fill `reward` directly or let `--custom-rm-path` compute it.
22	
23	The agent workflow itself may speak in strings, chat messages, tool calls, environment observations, or framework-specific events. The training target, however, should stay token based. Preserve the model-sampled token ids and use `loss_mask` to separate trainable model output from prompt, template, tool-observation, or environment text.
24	
25	If one prompt rollout corresponds to one training sample, return a single `Sample`. If one rollout splits into multiple trainable segments, such as subagent trajectories, main-agent continuations, or pre/post-compaction segments, return `list[Sample]` and set the same `rollout_id` on all sibling samples. slime then keeps those samples together for train-step splitting and loss aggregation instead of counting them as independent rollouts.
26	
27	Reach for `--rollout-function-path` only when you need to replace the whole rollout orchestration. Common reasons include custom data-source scheduling, cross-rollout background queues, fully asynchronous generation, or workflows that cannot fit the default `sglang_rollout` prompt-by-sample structure.
28	
29	## Agent Runtime Adapters
30	
31	slime includes protocol adapters for existing agent runtimes:
32	
33	- `slime.agent.adapters.AnthropicAdapter`: Anthropic Messages API, used by Claude Code style agents.
34	- `slime.agent.adapters.OpenAIAdapter`: OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses APIs, used by OpenAI SDK / OpenAI Agents SDK style clients.
35	
36	Adapters are a convenience layer, not a separate agent framework. Their contract is message history in, sampled tokens out: they render the chat template, call SGLang with `input_ids` and `return_logprob=True`, and export the returned token ids/logprobs as trainable trajectory segments. They avoid re-tokenizing response text to recover the training target.
37	
38	Instantiate the protocol-specific adapter in your custom generate function, run its `app` with aiohttp, then manage each rollout through the adapter instance:
39	
40	```python
41	from slime.agent.adapters import AnthropicAdapter
42	
43	adapter = AnthropicAdapter(
44	    tokenizer=tokenizer,
45	    sglang_url=sglang_url,
46	    tool_parser=tool_parser,
47	    reasoning_parser=reasoning_parser,
48	)
49	
50	adapter.open_session(session_id, sampling_defaults=sampling_params)
51	# Agent client sends requests to adapter.app.
52	segments = await adapter.finish_session(session_id)
53	```
54	
55	For multi-turn agents, use a stable `session_id`. The adapters pass it as `X-SMG-Routing-Key` so SGLang can route one session to the same worker and reuse prefix cache.
56	
57	## Agent Serving And Performance
58	
59	Agentic rollouts tend to depend more heavily on serving configuration than ordinary single-turn generation: contexts are longer, requests are multi-turn, latency has a heavier tail, and the workflow may need actor, reference, reward, or tool-side models at the same time.
60	
61	- Regular SGLang server arguments are passed as `--sglang-*`. For example, SGLang's `--context-length` becomes `--sglang-context-length`, and `--mem-fraction-static` becomes `--sglang-mem-fraction-static`.
62	- Router arguments are passed as `--router-*`. For multi-turn agents, consider `--router-policy consistent_hashing` so requests for the same `sample.session_id` go to the same worker and improve prefix-cache hit rate. See [Session-Affinity Routing for Multi-Turn Agents](../advanced/sglang-config.md#session-affinity-routing-for-multi-turn-agents).
63	- Use `--sglang-config` for more complex topologies: PD disaggregation, multi-model serving, heterogeneous server groups, and per-group SGLang overrides.
64	- For multi-turn or agentic RL, evaluate PD disaggregation. Prefill and decode have different workload shapes, and separating them makes it easier to scale each resource independently.
65	- For rollout-throughput optimization, also see [Speculative Decoding](../advanced/speculative-decoding.md) and [Low Precision Training](../advanced/low-precision.md).
66	
67	## Reference Example
68	
69	The full coding-agent example is [`examples/coding_agent_rl`](../_examples_synced/coding_agent_rl/README.md).
